objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with sudden loss of vision in one eye.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Doctor: What brings you in today? Patient: I suddenly lost vision in my right eye about half an hour ago while watching TV, and it hasn’t hurt at all.
Was the vision loss sudden and maximal at onset, or did it progress over a few minutes?
“It was sudden and felt maximal right away—there wasn’t any progression over minutes. It just happened while I was watching TV, and I noticed it immediately.”
Have you experienced any other symptoms such as flashes of light, floaters, or a curtain or shadow coming down over your vision in the affected eye?
“No, I haven’t had any flashes of light, new floaters, or a curtain or shadow coming down—just the sudden loss of vision in my right eye.”
Do you have a history of hypertension, diabetes, or any cardiovascular diseases?
Yes—I've had hypertension and type 2 diabetes, and I also have coronary artery disease. I’ve had trouble keeping up with my medications regularly.
Have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking since the vision loss occurred?
“No, I haven’t noticed any weakness or numbness on either side, and I haven’t had any trouble speaking.”
Have you experienced any pain on eye movement in the affected eye?
“No, there’s no pain when I move my right eye, and it hasn’t hurt at all.”
Have you had any recent trauma to your head or eye?
“No, I haven’t had any recent trauma to my head or my eye. I woke up feeling normal and then my right vision suddenly went away while I was watching TV.”

At this point, I have gathered sufficient information to consider a differential diagnosis.

[DDX] Central retinal artery occlusion, retinal detachment (less likely given the absence of flashes, floaters, or curtain/shadow), optic neuritis (less likely given the absence of pain), non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, stroke or transient ischemic attack (though less likely given the lack of other neurological symptoms)

However, given the format and the need to strictly follow it, I will reorder them according to likelihood based on the information provided.

[DDX] Central retinal artery occlusion, non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, retinal detachment, optic neuritis, stroke
